attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: A present-tense description of the integrations and the Samsung example. The proposition drops 'Samsung' but keeps the named example. 'Applications' is partly evaluative, and the contract flags this.

contract.note: Reading 'feature' as a capability built into an existing app, against a standalone product, is an ordinary reading given 'app integrations'. Limiting the test to the named example is fair. The unnamed integrations cannot be checked.

evidence.note: Samsung's January 2024 launch documentation says Live Translate is available only in the pre-installed Phone app. It is a company disclosure, but it is the source the contract prefers for product packaging.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's fair plain reading, contemporaneous Samsung documentation shows Live Translate was built into the existing Phone app, not shipped as a standalone application. That fits the feature-not-application characterisation for the named example. The unnamed integrations are not assessed.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: A compound present-tense observation: deeply unprofitable, and yet to prove its worth. The worth part is largely evaluative and vague. Separating out the 'public companies' clause is acceptable.

contract.note: The contract reasonably asks for aggregate net losses in Q4 2023 and a specified meaning of worth. The industry boundary, the threshold for 'deeply', and the meaning of worth are not supplied by the speaker, and the contract flags all three.

evidence.note: An OpenAI loss for 2022, one company in an earlier period, reported second-hand. It cannot establish aggregate losses in Q4 2023.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin, which includes non-AI services and is a gross figure, not net. A different metric and scope.
Productivity gains from a 2020–21 deployment. This bears on practical benefit, not on profitability, and refutes only a reading that denies all benefit.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no comparable industry-wide net profit-and-loss evidence for Q4 2023. The items cover a different period, a single firm, or a gross-margin metric. The worth component has no specified test, and the benefits evidence does not settle it. The evidence does not resolve the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own view: 'I firmly disagree — I think...'.

semantics.note: 'Will', together with 'firmly disagree', is firm expectation, not a hedge, so the claim is scored. Reading 'this stuff' as video with visible hallucinations fits the context. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Requiring representative audiences and strong offense tied to visual errors is a fair reading of 'regular people' and 'deeply offensive'. The referent of 'this stuff' is ambiguous, and the contract flags it.

evidence.note: Reports backlash to Coca-Cola's AI advert, but not from representative audiences and not tied to visual errors.

A single ad test found mostly positive emotions and little contempt. Respondents were not told the ad used AI, and it is unclear whether they noticed the errors. One campaign does not meet the early-resolution rule.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The early-resolution rule needs replicated, representative studies across several videos, and the packet has only reporting on one campaign, with mixed signals and errors not isolated. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion: 'we are rapidly approaching the top'.

semantics.note: An unhedged prediction that progress will soon slow sharply. 'Rapidly approaching' implies the near term but gives no date. The proposition captures it without adding conditions.

contract.note: Measuring capability progress across modalities is an ordinary reading. Adding no deadline is generous to the speaker, since 'rapidly approaching' implies soon, but it does not distort his words.

evidence.note: The 2026 AI Index reports rapid benchmark gains across domains in 2025 and growing video capability. This weighs against an imminent plateau, but it notes benchmark reliability problems, and under the contract it is not conclusive.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the contract says continuing gains cannot conclusively refute the forecast. The evidence shows rapid progress through 2025, which weighs against it. Nothing meets the early-resolution rule, which needs a sustained, broad slowdown. The claim stays unscored.
